newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen firmer in late trade, upside capped.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen firmer in late trade, upside capped.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures were firmer in late Thursday trade but the upside was capped by rate hike fears, dealers said.
They said the market was spooked by perceived hints of rate hikes by Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of Japan's International Finance Bureau.
Sentiment was further dampened by fairly neutral Bank of Japan (BOJ) monetary operations in the morning, which left a surplus of about 90 billion yen in the banking reserves.
But by late noon, rate hike fears subsided in Tokyo.
After hitting a low of 99.05, December Euroyen was trading around 99.09 at 1115 GMT against its IMM close of 99.05. Turnover was moderately active, around 14,405 lots.
Sakakibara's speech also undermined Japanese government bond (JGB) futures but they recovered in late trade.
June JGBs ended at 126.71 against 126.57 previously. Turnover was a paltry 192 lots.
"Trading was thin and is likely to continue to drift ahead of the Bank of Japan branch managers' meeting," said a Japanese dealer.
He said June JGBs saw keen buying at 126.52-126.60.
Activity on Eurodollars futures was subdued as the market awaited release of U.S. February trade data on Thursday.
September Eurodollars ended at 93.720 against its IMM close at 93.715 while December ended at 93.440 against its IMM close at 93.425.
Overall, the market was cautious ahead of the scheduled April 25 meeting between the U.S. President Bill Clinton and Japan Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
